title: 2.2. Operators: Data Operations Tools & Precedence
summary: Master arithmetic operators: addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), standard division (/), integer floor division (//), modulo (%), and exponentiation (**).
learningObjectives: Execute arithmetic operations and recognize which operations always produce float results.
Understand integer floor division (//) rounding down towards negative infinity.
Apply operator precedence hierarchy (PEMDAS) and associativity (left-to-right vs. right-to-left for **).

sections.heading: 2.2.1 The Arithmetic Operators
sections.content:
Python provides 7 primary arithmetic operators:
• + : Addition
• - : Subtraction
• * : Multiplication
• / : True Division — CRITICAL NETACAD RULE: The result of standard division (/) is ALWAYS a float, even if the division is exact (e.g. 6 / 3 produces 2.0).
• // : Integer Floor Division — Discards the fractional part and rounds down towards negative infinity (e.g. 6 // 4 is 1, but -6 // 4 is -2).
• % : Modulo (Remainder) — Computes the remainder after integer division (e.g. 14 % 4 is 2).
• ** : Exponentiation — Raises the left operand to the power of the right operand (e.g. 2 ** 3 is 8).

sections.heading: 2.2.2 Operator Precedence and Associativity
sections.content:
When multiple operators appear in a single expression, Python follows strict precedence rules:

1. Parentheses: () — Explicit grouping always evaluates first.
2. Exponentiation: ** — Right-to-left associativity (e.g. 2 ** 3 ** 2 = 2 ** 9 = 512, NOT 8 ** 2 = 64).
3. Unary operators: + (unary plus), - (unary minus).
4. Multiplicative operators: *, /, //, % — Left-to-right associativity.
5. Additive operators: +, - — Left-to-right associativity.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: What is the value of the Python expression: 2 ** 2 ** 3 ?

recap: Standard division (/) always yields a float. Exponentiation (**) uniquely binds from right to left.
